findings.reason: the plan should name `reckon/schema/flight.yaml` `fallback` and `reckon/crew/routing.py:resolve_budget_fallback` and state whether it extends or forks them, which changes §1's design.
findings.text: the plan adds a lane-routing decision without citing the existing declared-fallback mechanism; a reader cannot tell the new discharge search apart from the routing that already owns held-lane substitution

findings.reason: two backend-selection paths drift, and the declared-fallback owner is the mechanism a reader already expects to name the lane to use instead.
findings.text: §1's `_orchestrator_lane_discharge_candidates` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:4372) walks every configured backend and re-resolves it through `resolve_role_override` to find a usable alternative lane, duplicating `resolve_budget_fallback`, which already resolves a held backend's declared `fallback` for the same role; a backend already declares a substitution, so the honest change is to make the orchestrator lane discharge through that declaration (or extend it) rather than a second config scan beside it

findings.reason: the plan should extend the fence-waiver reason field to carry a second waiver class, or justify a parallel field; as written it adds a second reason-recording surface the discharge sibling plan (`an-orchestrator-can-discharge-a-refusal`) intends to own centrally.
findings.text: §2 proposes "a flag whose reason is recorded on the run and reaches the ledger row", which is exactly what `--no-fence REASON` already does (reckon/cli.py:1815 help: "record REASON on the run and its ledger row"; recorded at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:7475, carried to the ledger at reckon/crew/promotion.py:8517), yet the plan neither cites nor extends it

findings.reason: §2's override should be expressed in the sibling's discharge vocabulary or the two mechanisms will diverge on the shape of a recorded waiver.
findings.text: the override is designed without citing the waiver taxonomy its own sibling already fixes: `an-orchestrator-can-discharge-a-refusal` §4 defines a discharge as a waiver / alternative verdict / named owner, each "carrying the refusal's identity, the caller's stated reason, and a timestamp, onto a committed row", and `a-refusal-is-about-the-work` `plan-standalone` explicitly says the discharge work "stays with" that sibling

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the §1 stop is one cohesive concept composed in place (`_dispatch_orchestrator_lane_stop` plus its line renderer) inside the existing dispatch module; no new module and no spread of shallow wrappers over the same machinery.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the §1 discharge-candidate search re-implemented backend selection (`_orchestrator_lane_discharge_candidates` re-resolving every configured backend) rather than extending the declared-fallback routing its owner already provides.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites its sibling plans and the local-lane scanner, but never cites the two existing mechanisms its §1 discharge search and its §2 override each re-implement (`fallback` routing and `--no-fence REASON`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §2's override flag is a thin layer over the existing `--no-fence REASON` waiver-recording mechanism, with no statement of why that mechanism cannot be extended.
